prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one static Hearts of Iron IV stockpile-cost texticon, exact final canvas 30x12 pixels, shown inline beside a number.
Primary request: Create an original, nonfunctional miniature inventory glyph for a sealed hazardous-material canister in a strategy-game stockpile.
Subject: One squat horizontal pressure canister with rounded ends and a simple sealed cap; add one small muted yellow hazard triangle directly on the casing. The canister is only a symbolic icon. It has no opening, release feature, instructions, or visible contents.
Style/medium: Compact painted 2D inventory art with modest 1930s–1940s military materials, muted olive-drab and gunmetal, a small desaturated ochre hazard mark, restrained highlights, and a crisp dark edge.
Composition/framing: One centered broad horizontal object, about 2.4:1 width-to-height, designed to remain distinct beside numeric text at 30x12. Use a centered horizontal strip on the source canvas, a simple silhouette, inset complete edges, and transparent margin.
Lighting/mood: Even understated icon lighting with small metallic highlights only.
Constraints: Genuinely transparent unused canvas; no scene or floor; no text, letters, numbers, watermark, fumes, extra objects, tile, frame, border, badge, medallion, or separate emblem. The hazard mark is painted directly on the canister. Optimize for smooth downsampling to 30x12.
Avoid: Fuel-can shape, missile or bomb silhouette, bright neon colors, chrome shine, modern equipment, cinematic lighting, fake checkerboard, opaque matte, colored halo, clipped edges, unintended transparent holes.
